text:
SCHOLARSHIPS (checked 4 November 2026)

Key rules that decide most eligibility questions:
- Deutschlandstipendium: 300 EUR per month (150 federal, 150 private sponsor), awarded by the university for at least two semesters (one year), renewable. All nationalities, new and current students, Bachelor's and Master's, at participating public and state-recognised universities (including private ones such as HMKW and Macromedia). Funding is only paid within the standard period of study (Regelstudienzeit) of the current degree, so a student in the final semester of the standard period normally cannot receive it, because the next award round starts after their standard period ends. It cannot be combined with another merit scholarship above 30 EUR per month on average; jobs, BAfoeG and need-based help are fine. Selection: grades plus engagement and personal circumstances. Each university runs its own call, usually once a year (HMKW awards every winter semester; applicants and full-time students can apply via studienberatung@hmkw.de).
- DAAD STIBET graduation grants (Studienabschlussbeihilfe / Abschlussstipendium): short grants from a university's International Office for international students in their final phase (often the last 1 to 2 semesters) with good results and financial need. Availability depends on the university, mainly public and state-recognised ones with DAAD STIBET funds. This is the usual option for students who are too late for the Deutschlandstipendium.
- Foundations (Boell, Adenauer, Ebert, Rosa Luxemburg, KAAD) fund for the remaining standard period too, so they also do not help in the very last semester.
- A scholarship award letter that covers the required monthly amount can replace the blocked account for the visa (confirm with the German Mission).

### DAAD Study Scholarships: Fine Art, Design, Visual Communication and Film (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-art]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master; fields: Fine art, graphic and communication design, visual communication, illustration, animation, film
Pays: €992 per month. Covers: €992 per month for living costs; Travel allowance; One-off study allowance; Health, accident and liability insurance; German course (2 to 6 months) if your program is in German; Rent or family allowance in some cases. Not covered: Tuition fees (most public art and design schools charge none)
Who can apply: A first university degree in fine art, design, visual communication or film; Usually graduated within the last 6 years; A strong artistic portfolio: it counts more than your grades; Language of the course (German or English) by the start of the scholarship
Documents: DAAD portal application form; CV; Study plan and motivation letter; Transcripts and degree certificate; Portfolio: DAAD asks for it after a first formal check; Admission letter from the German school before the scholarship starts
How to apply: Choose a Master's or postgraduate course at a German art, design or film school > Apply on the DAAD portal before the deadline (from Pakistan: generally end of November) > Upload the portfolio when DAAD asks for it > A committee of German art and design professors decides, usually within about 7 months > Apply to the school itself in parallel; the scholarship does not give admission
Deadline: From Pakistan: generally end of November each year, for study from October the next year. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.daad.pk/en/find-funding/scholarship-database/2/?type=a&origin=194&subjectgroup=0&q=0&status=0&onlydaad=0&language=en&id=0&pg=2&detail_to_show=57135742 | apply: https://portal.daad.de
Tip: If you studied design, this is the best scholarship in Germany for you. Put your strongest 10 to 15 projects first.

### DAAD EPOS: Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-epos]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: Economics, public health, engineering, water, energy, agriculture, environment, urban planning, public policy (only courses on the EPOS list)
Pays: €992 per month (Master's), €1,400 per month (PhD). Covers: Monthly stipend; Health, accident and liability insurance; Travel allowance; Rent subsidy or family allowance in some cases; Funding for 12 to 42 months depending on the course
Who can apply: At least 2 years of professional work experience after your Bachelor's; A Bachelor's degree, usually 4 years, with results in about the top third; Pakistan is an eligible country; Clear motivation to work on development in Pakistan after the degree
Documents: DAAD application form (signed); CV in Europass format; Motivation letter about your development goals; Employer letter confirming work experience; Recommendation letters (usually 2); Degree and transcripts with HEC attestation; Language certificate (IELTS or TOEFL, level set by the course)
How to apply: Pick up to 3 courses from the official EPOS list > Apply directly to each course by its own deadline, and mark that you want an EPOS scholarship > The university shortlists and proposes candidates to DAAD > DAAD makes the final decision
Deadline: Each course has its own deadline. For the 2027/28 intake most closed between August and October 2026, some run into early 2027. Check the course list.. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.daad.pk/en/find-funding/scholarship-database/?type=a&origin=194&subjectgroup=0&q=epos&status=0&page=0&onlydaad=1&language=en&id=0&pg=1&detail_to_show=50076777 | apply: https://static.daad.de/media/daad_de/pdfs_nicht_barrierefrei/in-deutschland-studieren-forschen-lehren/daad_epos_deadlines.pdf
Tip: Work experience is not optional here. Two years in an NGO, government office, hospital or engineering firm makes you a strong candidate.

### DAAD Helmut Schmidt Programme (Public Policy and Good Governance) (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-hsp]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master; fields: Public policy, governance, public administration, development, peace and conflict studies, at selected partner universities
Pays: €992 per month. Covers: Monthly stipend; Health insurance; Travel and study allowances; Language course before the program
Who can apply: A very good Bachelor's degree, usually finished within the last 6 years; Interest and engagement in public policy, social justice or governance; Work or volunteer experience helps a lot; English proficiency for the chosen course
Documents: Application through the DAAD portal for the chosen partner university; CV; Motivation letter linked to Pakistan's governance or social challenges; Recommendation letters; Degree and transcripts; English certificate
How to apply: Choose up to 3 Master's courses from the programme list > Apply in the window, generally 1 June to the end of July > The universities and DAAD select together > Results usually come in the following spring
Deadline: From Pakistan: generally end of July each year, for study from the next autumn. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.daad.pk/en/find-funding/scholarship-database/4/?type=a&origin=194&subjectgroup=0&q=0&status=0&onlydaad=0&language=en&id=0&pg=4&detail_to_show=50026397 | apply: https://portal.daad.de
Tip: Write about a real problem you have seen in Pakistan and how this Master's helps you solve it.

### DAAD Study Scholarships: Architecture (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-arch]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master; fields: Architecture, interior architecture, urban and regional planning, landscape architecture, monument conservation
Pays: €992 per month. Covers: Monthly stipend; Travel allowance; Insurance; German course if needed
Who can apply: A first degree in architecture or a related field; Usually graduated within the last 6 years; A portfolio of your work
Documents: DAAD portal application; CV; Motivation letter and study plan; Portfolio; Transcripts and degree; Recommendation letter
How to apply: Choose a Master's or postgraduate course > Apply on the DAAD portal > Submit the portfolio > Apply to the university in parallel
Deadline: From Pakistan: generally end of September each year. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.daad.pk/en/find-funding/scholarship-database/2/?type=a&origin=194&subjectgroup=0&q=0&status=0&onlydaad=0&language=en&id=0&pg=2&detail_to_show=57135744 | apply: https://portal.daad.de

### DAAD Study Scholarships: Music and Performing Arts (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-music]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master; fields: Music, drama, directing, dance, choreography, performance
Pays: €992 per month. Covers: Monthly stipend; Travel allowance; Insurance; German course if needed
Who can apply: A first degree in music or performing arts; Recordings or work samples of high quality
Documents: DAAD portal application; CV; Motivation letter; Recordings or videos; Transcripts and degree
How to apply: Choose a course at a German music or arts school > Apply on the DAAD portal > Send recordings when asked
Deadline: From Pakistan: Music generally at the start of October, Performing Arts at the end of October. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.daad.pk/en/find-funding/scholarship-database/2/?type=a&origin=194&subjectgroup=0&q=0&status=0&onlydaad=0&language=en&id=0&pg=2&detail_to_show=57135743 | apply: https://portal.daad.de

### DAAD Doctoral Programmes in Germany (full PhD) (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-phd]
Type: fully funded; levels: PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: €1,400 per month. Covers: Monthly stipend for up to 3 years, sometimes 4; Research allowance; Travel allowance; Insurance; German course
Who can apply: A Master's or MS/MPhil degree with very good results; A research proposal; A supervisor in Germany who agrees to supervise you (or admission to a structured doctoral program)
Documents: DAAD portal application; CV; Research proposal and timetable; Supervisor's letter of support; Degrees and transcripts; Recommendation letter from a professor in Pakistan; Language certificate
How to apply: Find a supervisor first: email professors with a short proposal > Prepare the proposal with the supervisor's input > Apply on the DAAD portal by the Pakistan deadline > Interviews and results usually by the following spring
Deadline: From Pakistan: generally end of August each year (31 August 2026 for funding in 2027). Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: http://daad.de/go/en/stipa57135739 | apply: https://portal.daad.de
Tip: HEC Pakistan also announces this call. Finding the supervisor takes months, so start early.

### DAAD Research Grants (2 to 12 months) (DAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=daad-research]
Type: fully funded; levels: PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: €1,400 per month. Covers: Monthly stipend; Travel allowance; Insurance
Who can apply: You are doing a PhD in Pakistan and want to research part of it in Germany; A host professor in Germany
Documents: DAAD portal application; Research proposal; Host's letter; CV; Supervisor's recommendation in Pakistan
How to apply: Agree a project with a German host > Apply on the DAAD portal by the deadline
Deadline: From Pakistan: generally end of August each year. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: http://daad.de/go/en/stipa57742121 | apply: https://portal.daad.de

### Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (European Union) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=erasmus]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master; fields: Over 100 programs, from data science to food science. You study in 2 or more European countries, often including Germany.
Pays: €1,400 per month. Covers: €1,400 per month for the whole program (12 to 24 months); Tuition fees; Travel, visa and installation costs; Health insurance
Who can apply: A Bachelor's degree (final year students can often apply); English proficiency (usually IELTS 6.5 or equal); You have not had an Erasmus Mundus scholarship before
Documents: Online application to each program (consortium); CV; Motivation letter; 2 recommendation letters; Degree and transcripts; English certificate; Passport copy
How to apply: Browse the official catalogue and pick up to 3 programs > Apply to each program directly on its own website > Each program ranks applicants and offers the scholarships
Deadline: Each program sets its own. Most close between October and January for the following September.. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/opportunities/opportunities-for-individuals/students/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters
Tip: Many January deadlines. Start your motivation letters now.

### Heinrich Böll Foundation Scholarship (Heinrich Böll Foundation) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=boell]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: Monthly stipend in line with the German student grant rates (about €992 for Master's in 2026), more for PhD. Covers: Monthly stipend; Health insurance contribution; Seminars and a strong network
Who can apply: Very good academic results; Social or political engagement in line with green values (ecology, democracy, human rights); Admission or enrolment at a German university; Usually good German skills are expected; check the language rules for your case
Documents: Online application; CV; Motivation letter about your engagement; Recommendation letters; Degree and transcripts; Admission letter or proof of enrolment
How to apply: Get admission to a German university > Apply online in the window (portal opens about 6 weeks before the deadline) > Interview with a liaison lecturer, then a selection committee
Deadline: Twice a year: 1 March and 1 September. Apply from Pakistan: usually only once admitted or enrolled in Germany. German needed: yes
Official: https://www.boell.de/en/scholarships

### Konrad Adenauer Foundation Scholarship for international students (Konrad Adenauer Foundation) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=kas]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: €992 per month (Master's) or €1,400 per month (PhD), 2026 rates. Covers: Monthly stipend; Health insurance allowance; Seminars and mentoring
Who can apply: Excellent grades and social or political engagement; Identification with democratic, Christian Democratic values; Good German (around B2 or higher); Usually under 30
Documents: Online application on the KAS portal; CV; Motivation letter; Recommendation letters; Degree and transcripts; German certificate
How to apply: Apply online > Selection interview > Funding usually starts with the next winter semester
Deadline: Annual. Around 15 July for applicants already in Germany; applicants from abroad may have an earlier round. Confirm on kas.de.. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: yes
Official: https://www.kas.de/en/scholarships

### Friedrich Ebert Foundation Scholarship for international students (Friedrich Ebert Foundation) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=fes]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: €992 per month (Master's), more for PhD. Covers: Monthly stipend; Health insurance contribution; Seminars
Who can apply: Very good results; Social engagement in line with social democratic values; German at least B2; Admission or enrolment at a German university
Documents: Online application (mostly in German); CV; Motivation letter; Recommendation letters; Transcripts; German certificate
How to apply: Apply online once you have or expect admission > Interviews > Decision
Deadline: Usually twice a year, around 30 November and 31 May. Confirm on fes.de.. Apply from Pakistan: usually only once admitted or enrolled in Germany. German needed: yes
Official: https://www.fes.de/en/studienfoerderung/international-applicants

### Rosa Luxemburg Foundation Scholarship (Rosa Luxemburg Foundation) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=rls]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: Monthly stipend at German student grant rates. Covers: Monthly stipend; Seminars
Who can apply: Social and political engagement, especially for social justice; Good grades; German skills; Preference for women and students from non-academic families
Documents: Online application; CV; Motivation letter; Recommendations; Transcripts
How to apply: Apply online > Interviews > Decision
Deadline: Twice a year: 1 April and 1 October. Apply from Pakistan: usually only once admitted or enrolled in Germany. German needed: yes
Official: https://www.rosalux.de/stiftung/studienwerk/studienstipendium/

### KAAD Scholarship (Catholic Academic Exchange Service) (KAAD) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=kaad]
Type: fully funded; levels: Master, PhD; fields: All subjects
Pays: Monthly stipend at DAAD-like rates. Covers: Monthly stipend; Travel; Insurance; German course up to 6 months
Who can apply: Mainly for Catholic students and graduates from Asia, Africa, the Middle East and Latin America; Applications go through KAAD's partner committee in your country; Work experience is preferred
Documents: KAAD questionnaire; CV; Motivation letter and study plan; Transcripts and degree; Recommendations
How to apply: Contact KAAD's partner in Pakistan > Fill the online questionnaire > Selection committees meet twice a year
Deadline: Through the partner committee in Pakistan, usually by mid year. Confirm with KAAD.. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.kaad.de/stipendien/stipendienprogramm-1 | apply: https://www.kaad-application.de/

### Deutschlandstipendium (German government and private sponsors, through your university) [Raasta page: https://raheelgul063-lgtm.github.io/raasta/#/scholarship?id=deutschland]
Type: partial; levels: Bachelor, Master; fields: All subjects, at public and state-recognised universities (including many private ones)
Pays: €300 per month. Covers: €300 per month for at least 1 year, renewable; Mentoring and networking with sponsors at many universities. Not covered: Not enough to replace the blocked account on its own
Who can apply: All nationalities, new students and current students; Good grades plus engagement (volunteering, family duties, overcoming obstacles); No other merit scholarship above €30 per month
Documents: Application on your university's portal; CV; Motivation letter; Transcripts; Proof of engagement; Sometimes a recommendation
How to apply: Check if your university takes part (most do) > Watch the university's call, often in spring or summer for the winter semester > Apply through the university; a committee decides
Deadline: Set by each university, usually once a year. Apply from Pakistan: yes. German needed: not always
Official: https://www.deutschlandstipendium.de/de/english-1700.html
Tip: Most international students never apply, so your chances are better than you think.

Private university scholarships:
- University of Europe for Applied Sciences (UE): Cultural Diversity Scholarship: 50% off first year tuition; Women in Tech Scholarship for tech programs; Digital Pioneers Scholarship: €1,000; Industry scholarships with partners such as JobTeaser for Visual Communication and UX/UI Design. How: Fill the UE scholarship form and send it to student.advice@ue-germany.com before you sign the study agreement. Page: https://ue-germany.com/study-with-us/fees-and-finance/ue-scholarships
- Gisma University of Applied Sciences: Women in Tech: four 100% and twelve 50% scholarships per year; High Achievers Scholarship for South Asian applicants, applied automatically from your grades; Siblings and spouse discount: 35%. How: Ask your Gisma programme consultant during the application. Page: https://www.gisma.com/life-at-gisma/tuition-fees-and-funding
- Arden University Berlin: Berlin Merit Scholarship for Bachelor's programs (applied automatically if you meet the criteria); Regional pricing for Master's and MBA programs. How: Applied automatically when you meet the criteria. Page: https://arden.ac.uk/berlin/admissions/fees/international-scholarships-berlin
- Macromedia University of Applied Sciences: Excellence Scholarship for very strong grades (courses or a tuition reduction); Macromedia Scholarship for artistic talent and difficult financial situations; Deutschlandstipendium. How: Email the documents to the International Student Advisory Service with or after your program application. Page: https://www.macromedia-fachhochschule.de/en/advisory/fees-financing/scholarships/
- Berlin School of Business and Innovation (BSBI): Changing programme offers and tuition discounts for international students. How: Discounts are usually applied with your offer; ask admissions which one fits. Page: https://www.berlinsbi.com/studying-at-bsbi/programme-offers
- HMKW University of Applied Sciences for Media, Communication and Management: Deutschlandstipendium every winter semester, open to applicants and students. How: Email studienberatung@hmkw.de with the subject "Deutschlandstipendium". Page: https://www.hmkw.de/en/university/departments/journalism-and-communication/news/journalism-news/news/vergabe-der-deutschlandstipendien0
- IU International University of Applied Sciences: Tuition reductions for on-campus programs that change by intake. How: Ask the IU admissions team which reduction applies when you apply. Page: https://www.iu.org
- EU Business School Munich: Merit and need based tuition scholarships. How: Ask admissions before you accept your offer. Page: https://www.euruni.edu

Already studying in Germany:
- Deutschlandstipendium: €300 per month, open to international students at most universities. Apply through your university once a year.
- DAAD STIBET and graduation scholarships: Short scholarships from your university's International Office, often for students in their final semesters or with special engagement.
- DAAD Prize: €1,000 award for an outstanding international student at each university, nominated by professors.
- Political and church foundations: Böll, Adenauer, Ebert, Rosa Luxemburg and KAAD also fund students already enrolled in Germany. German skills help a lot here.
- Studierendenwerk emergency help: If you have a sudden money problem, the student services office and the International Office can help with small grants or loans.

How to apply in general:
- 12 to 15 months before you start: Shortlist programs and scholarships together. Many deadlines are a year before the course starts (DAAD art and design: November; Helmut Schmidt: July).
- Get your documents ready: HEC attested degree and transcripts, IELTS or TOEFL, a Europass CV, and 2 recommendation letters from teachers or employers. Recommenders need weeks, so ask early.
- Write one strong story: Every scholarship asks: why this program, why Germany, and what will you do for Pakistan afterwards. Use real examples, not big words.
- Apply to several: Apply for 2 or 3 scholarships and to the universities in parallel. A scholarship rarely gives admission by itself.
- Plan for both outcomes: Results often come 4 to 7 months later. If you win, a scholarship letter covering the required monthly amount can replace the blocked account for your visa (confirm with the German Mission). If not, keep your self-funded plan ready.

Documents usually needed: Passport; Degree and transcripts with HEC attestation (Intermediate and Matric certificates for Bachelor's applicants); IELTS, TOEFL or another accepted English test; German certificate for German-taught programs and most foundations; CV in Europass format; Motivation letter or statement of purpose; 2 recommendation letters; Employer letter for work experience (EPOS and Helmut Schmidt); Portfolio for design, art, architecture and film; Research proposal and supervisor's letter for a PhD; Admission letter or proof of application, when asked

STUDENT JOBS
Work rules: Non EU students may work 140 full days or 280 half days per year. During the semester, Werkstudent jobs are limited to 20 hours a week. Mini jobs pay up to €603 per month without taxes or social security. The minimum wage in 2026 is €13.90 per hour.
Shift apps: Zenjob, Jobvalley, StudentJob, Coople, Instaff. Agencies: TimePartner, ManpowerGroup, Randstad, Adecco, Hays, Persona service.

MOVING TO GERMANY
- Registration (Anmeldung) and tax ID: Register your address at the local Bürgeramt within 14 days of moving in. Bring your passport and the landlord confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung). You get a registration certificate (Meldebescheinigung). Banks, the foreigners office and your blocked account payout need it. Your tax ID (Steuer-ID) arrives by post a few weeks after your first registration. Keep it: every employer needs it. Book Bürgeramt appointments online as early as possible; in big cities slots are scarce.
- Health and other insurance: Statutory student health insurance costs about €141 to €146 per month in 2026, almost the same at every public insurer. Popular with international students: TK, AOK, Barmer, DAK, hkk. Your university needs an insurance confirmation before it enrols you, so sign up right after admission. Private insurance only makes sense in special cases; if you opt out of statutory insurance you usually cannot switch back while studying. Personal liability insurance (Haftpflichtversicherung) is cheap and strongly recommended: it covers damage you cause to others or to your apartment.
- Housing and avoiding scams: Apply for a Studierendenwerk dorm as soon as you are admitted; they are the cheapest option and have waiting lists. Shared flats (WG): WG-Gesucht.de is the main site. Apartments: ImmoScout24, Kleinanzeigen. Scam warning signs: the landlord is abroad and sends keys by post, asks for money before a viewing, wants Western Union or crypto, or the price is far below the market. Never pay a deposit before you have a signed contract. The deposit (Kaution) is legally capped at three months of cold rent. Rent for a 30 m² student flat (MLP report 2026): about €880 in Munich, €725 in Berlin, €700 to €720 in Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Heidelberg. Eastern cities such as Chemnitz and Magdeburg are far cheaper.
- Money and bank accounts: Your blocked account pays €992 per month into a normal German current account (Girokonto), so open one in your first week. Online banks (N26, DKB) open quickly with just a passport. Traditional banks (Sparkasse, Commerzbank, Deutsche Bank) have branches and free student accounts but may need your registration certificate. Many shops and restaurants still prefer cash or the German debit card (Girocard). Carry some cash. Working: non EU students may work 140 full days or 280 half days per year. Student jobs (Werkstudent) up to 20 hours a week during the semester.
- Student jobs, apps and agencies: Work rules: 140 full days or 280 half days per year; Werkstudent jobs up to 20 hours a week during the semester; mini jobs up to €603 per month. Shift apps: Zenjob, Jobvalley, Coople, Instaff. Choose your own shifts and get paid quickly. Staffing agencies: TimePartner, ManpowerGroup, Randstad, Adecco, Hays and Persona service place students in logistics, office, industry and IT jobs. Job portals: LinkedIn, StepStone, Indeed, XING and the official Arbeitsagentur Jobbörse. See the full list with links on the Jobs page. Never pay to get a job. Real agencies are paid by employers.
- Mobile and internet: Prepaid SIM cards (no contract) from Aldi Talk, Lidl Connect, Congstar or fraenk are cheap and flexible. You must verify your identity with your passport. The big networks are Telekom, Vodafone and O2. Discount brands use the same networks at lower prices. Home internet contracts often run 24 months. In a WG, internet is usually shared and included in the rent; check before signing.
- Transport: Most universities include the Deutschlandsemesterticket in the semester fee: unlimited local and regional transport across Germany. It costs 60% of the Deutschlandticket (€63 per month in 2026). Without a semester ticket, the Deutschlandticket costs €63 per month and covers all local buses, trams, U-Bahn, S-Bahn and regional trains in Germany. Long distance ICE and IC trains are not included. Book early on DB Navigator for cheap saver fares. Cycling is common: use bike lanes and lights at night, or you can be fined.
- Daily life: shops and apps: Cheapest supermarkets: Aldi, Lidl, Penny, Netto. Larger choice: Rewe, Edeka, Kaufland. Drugstores: dm and Rossmann. Halal meat and South Asian spices: Turkish and Arab grocery stores in every city; Asian stores for rice, lentils and spices. Shops are closed on Sundays and public holidays, except some at main train stations. Essential apps: DB Navigator, your city transport app, WG-Gesucht, Kleinanzeigen, Doctolib (doctor appointments), PayPal, Too Good To Go, Google Maps.
- Culture and norms: Be on time. Arriving even 5 minutes late to a meeting, class or appointment is seen as impolite. Recycling is taken seriously: yellow bin for packaging, blue for paper, brown for organic, black for the rest. Return bottles with Pfand for your deposit back. Quiet hours (Ruhezeit) are usually 22:00 to 06:00 and all day on Sundays. No loud music or drilling. Do not cross at a red pedestrian light, even if the street is empty, especially when children are around. Germans are direct: a clear no is not rude. Use Sie (formal you) with professors and officials until they offer du.
- Leisure: With the semester ticket, weekend trips by regional train cost nothing extra: lakes, castles, old towns and other cities. Join university sports (Hochschulsport): cheap classes from cricket to climbing. Many cities have Pakistani student associations. Christmas markets in December, beer gardens and lakes in summer, and cheap flights across Europe from major airports. Many museums have free or cheap student entry; always carry your student ID.

CITIES
- Berlin: rent about €725; employers Siemens, Deutsche Bahn, Zalando, Delivery Hero, HelloFresh
- Munich: rent about €880; employers BMW, Siemens, Allianz, Munich Re, Infineon
- Hamburg: rent about €700 to €720; employers Airbus, Hapag-Lloyd, HHLA (Port of Hamburg), Otto Group, Beiersdorf
- Frankfurt: rent about €721; employers Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, European Central Bank, Deutsche Börse, Fraport
- Cologne: rent about €700 to €720; employers Ford Europe, REWE Group, RTL, Lanxess, AXA
- Stuttgart: rent null; employers Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, Bosch, Trumpf, Daimler Truck
- Aachen: rent null; employers RWTH Aachen spin-offs, FEV, Ford Research Center, Ericsson, Fraunhofer institutes
- Darmstadt: rent about €599; employers Merck, ESA ESOC, EUMETSAT, Deutsche Telekom, Software AG
- Dresden: rent null; employers Infineon, GlobalFoundries, Bosch, ESMC (TSMC joint venture), Volkswagen
- Leipzig: rent null; employers BMW, Porsche, DHL Hub Leipzig, Amazon, Siemens Energy
- Karlsruhe: rent null; employers SAP (Walldorf, nearby), EnBW, dm-drogerie markt, Bosch, KIT spin-offs
- Hannover: rent null; employers Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles, Continental, Hannover Re, TUI, Deutsche Messe
